title: Nonzero-temperature vibronic spectra of polyatomic molecules from a zero-temperature classical trajectory
authors: Davide Barbiero, Jiří J. L. Vaníček
abstract: By combining coherence thermofield dynamics with the single-Hessian approximation, we enable simulations of low- to medium-resolution vibronic spectra of weakly anharmonic systems at nonzero temperatures, at negligible additional cost relative to zero-temperature calculations. Single-Hessian coherence thermofield Gaussian wavepacket dynamics is exact in any harmonic potential, provided that the reference Hessian is that of the final surface. When applied to Morse systems of increasing anharmonicity and varying temperature, this method successfully captures excited-state anharmonicity and key temperature-dependent spectral features, including hot bands and broadening. By combining the method with on-the-fly ab initio dynamics, we demonstrate its utility by computing the absorption spectra of naphthalene, aminocoumarin C450, and phenyl radical, and the photoelectron spectrum of SeO$_{2}^{-}$ . Within the ab initio single-Hessian approximation, after the zero-temperature spectrum is obtained at the cost of classical molecular dynamics (on the order of hours), all nonzero-temperature spectra are computed in seconds.
summary: This paper introduces a novel computational method combining coherence thermofield dynamics and the single-Hessian approximation to simulate vibronic spectra of polyatomic molecules at finite temperatures. It demonstrates that this approach accurately captures temperature effects like hot bands while maintaining computational efficiency by reusing a single zero-temperature trajectory. The method is successfully applied to compute spectra for several benchmark molecules.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of simulating low- to medium-resolution vibronic spectra of weakly anharmonic polyatomic molecules at nonzero temperatures.
main_result: The proposed single-Hessian coherence thermofield Gaussian wavepacket dynamics method successfully captures temperature-dependent spectral features like hot bands and broadening with high accuracy.
method: The core method combines coherence thermofield dynamics with the single-Hessian approximation to propagate a Gaussian wavepacket in an augmented configuration space.
model_or_system: The method is tested on polyatomic molecules, validated using Morse systems, and applied to compute spectra for naphthalene, aminocoumarin C450, phenyl radical, and the photoelectron spectrum of SeO2.
key_observables: Absorption cross-section $\sigma(\omega)$, photoelectron spectra, and vibronic spectra intensity vs. wavenumber ($	ext{cm}^{-1}$).
important_parameters: Nonzero temperatures (e.g., 700 K), anharmonicity levels, and the choice of reference Hessian.
main_assumptions: The method relies on the single-Hessian approximation, the electric dipole approximation, the first-order time-dependent perturbation theory, and the Condon approximation.
figures_summary: Figures compare spectra from various methods (adiabatic harmonic, local harmonic, single-Hessian GWD) for molecules like BaS, SeO2, and naphthalene, demonstrating the single-Hessian method's superior performance across different temperatures.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the theoretical framework, validates it using simple models (Morse), compares its results against established methods (adiabatic harmonic, local harmonic) across varying temperatures, and applies it to several complex molecular systems (naphthalene, SeO2, etc.).
why_interesting: This work provides a computationally efficient and accurate theoretical tool for calculating temperature-dependent spectra, which is crucial for understanding molecular dynamics and energy transfer in condensed phases.
